projects.title: Determining an optimal game strategy using a genetic algorithm
projects.description:
I wanted to see if there was an optimal strategy to play a very simple PC game from 2004 called Porrasturvat. I decided to try using a genetic algorithm to accomplish this, which would mean I would either have to do it manually, which has a lot of room for error, or to automate the process. The game is a binary Windows program, so to automate it requires sending keyboard inputs to the game window, as well as modifying and reading memory to determine and set the game's state.

I determined that I could do this with a Python script, using the ctypes library to utilize Windows's kernel32.dll to read and write memory. I had to use the pyautogui library to send keyboard inputs to the game, and user32.dll via ctypes to determine if the game's window was in focus.

After setting up the genetic algorithm based on what I'd learned at college, once I got everything working, I just ran the script to see what would happen. In a few minutes, the genetic algorithm had figured out a strategy that was better than any I had been able to do. While it was a simple game, the results were still very cool, considering that the script knew nothing of how the game worked at all.
